The role can be located in either Dallas, TX or Austin, TX and this position acts as a vital liaison in the field, fostering collaboration among contractors, design consultants, and project teams to ensure seamless delivery and project success. The Resident Construction Manager will monitor day-to-day construction activities and provide leadership in resolving field issues while maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality, schedule, cost control, and successful project delivery. The position requires extensive field presence and the ability to work effectively in active rail, transit, roadway, and transportation environments. Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in: Serve as the primary on-site construction management representative for assigned rail, transit, roadway, and infrastructure projects. Provide daily oversight of contractor construction activities, including civil, structural, track, stations, drainage, utilities, roadway, bridges, systems, facilities, and other transportation-related work as applicable. Monitor contractor performance to ensure compliance with contract documents, drawings, specifications, approved submittals, and applicable standards. Review construction schedules, monitor progress, identify potential delays, and work with contractors and project teams to develop recovery strategies. Coordinate daily activities among contractors, subcontractors, design consultants, utilities, public agencies, operations and maintenance personnel, and other project stakeholders. Monitor construction quality and verify that work is performed in accordance with approved plans, specifications, inspection requirements, and quality-control procedures. Coordinate and document inspections, testing, punch-list activities, substantial completion, final acceptance, and project closeout. Review and track RFIs, submittals, change requests, field directives, non-conformance issues, and other construction documentation. Identify potential construction issues early and facilitate timely resolution with the contractor, designer, and project management team. Review contractor pay applications and quantities for accuracy and confirm that work has been completed in accordance with the contract. Monitor project costs, changes, claims, and potential impacts to the project budget. Maintain accurate daily reports, inspection records, photographs, correspondence, meeting records, and other project documentation. Participate in progress meetings, coordination meetings, safety meetings, and stakeholder meetings. Coordinate construction activities that may affect rail operations, transit service, roadways, pedestrian access, utilities, public facilities, and adjacent properties. Ensure appropriate work-zone controls, traffic-control measures, public safety measures, and railroad/transit protection requirements are implemented. Coordinate with operations and maintenance personnel to minimize impacts to existing transportation services, facilities, and infrastructure. Monitor contractor safety performance and immediately escalate unsafe conditions or activities. Assist with review and implementation of construction sequencing, work plans, outage plans, maintenance-of-traffic plans, and temporary conditions. Support testing, startup, integration, and commissioning activities for completed facilities and systems. Assist project management with claims evaluation, negotiations, risk management, and resolution of construction disputes. Provide technical input regarding constructability, sequencing, field conditions, and proposed design changes. Support project turnover, record documentation, as-built verification, warranty activities, and final closeout. What you will bring to the Team: Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, Transportation Engineering, or a related field preferred. 15+ years of progressive construction management experience, preferably on major transportation, transit, railroad, roadway, or infrastructure projects. Experience serving in an owner’s representative, resident engineer, resident construction manager, construction manager, or similar field leadership role. Experience in the rail construction industry is critical. Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, schedules, contracts, and technical documents. Experience with commuter rail, light rail, heavy rail, railroad, transit, roadway, bridge, or other major transportation infrastructure projects. Experience working on projects involving active rail operations, transit service, roadways, or other operating transportation facilities. Experience with track, stations, signals, communications, traction power, grade crossings, roadway improvements, bridges, drainage, utilities, facilities, or transit systems. Experience with TxDOT, FTA, FRA, FHWA, APTA, or other applicable transportation, transit, and infrastructure standards and requirements. Experience with Primavera P6 or other scheduling platforms. Experience with document management and construction management platforms such as Procore, Autodesk Construction Cloud, e-Builder, or similar systems. Professional Engineer (PE), CCM, DBIA, or other relevant professional certification is a plus. Translate regulatory requirements, supervisory feedback and audit findings into clearly scoped projects with defined deliverables, milestones, owners and success criteria. Build and maintain integrated project plans, RAID logs, dependency maps and resource plans, ensuring delivery is accurate, complete and on time. Manage scope, change control and prioritisation across concurrent regulatory initiatives, escalating conflicts and trade-offs early. Ensure project outputs are embedded into business-as-usual operations, with documented processes, controls and clear handover to accountable owners. Ensure delivery remains compliant with applicable laws, CBI/EBA guidance, FCA requirements and Firm policy. Ensure remediation evidence (MI packs, service review records, complaints reconciliation, AML assurance outputs and enforcement actions) is captured and audit-ready at project close. Supervisory, Audit & Regulatory Commitments Own the plan for delivering regulatory commitments, supervisory actions and audit findings within scope, tracking progress to timely and evidenced closure. Coordinate preparation of regulatory submissions, evidence packs and operational responses, ensuring deadlines are met and quality is consistent. Act as a senior first-line project contact for regulatory reviews, audits and assurance activity, working in partnership with Risk and Compliance. Ensure consistent project approach and delivery standards across Ireland and the UK. Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Management Establish and run project governance, including steering groups, working groups. Maintain decision logs and clear escalation routes. Produce concise, accurate status reporting for Senior Management, Committees and the Board on regulatory project progress, risks and issues. Manage a broad stakeholder group across Operations, Compliance, Risk, Legal, Finance, Technology, Client Management and third parties, holding contributors to agreed commitments. Act under delegated authority, where required, to represent regulatory projects in regulatory, audit and internal governance forums. Delivery Capability & Continuous Improvement Support and complement the COO Ireland by providing senior delivery leadership across regulatory change and remediation. Contribute to the design of a scalable, repeatable approach to regulatory change delivery. Capture lessons learned and drive process efficiency, simplification and automation opportunities identified through project work. Coach and guide project contributors, building project delivery discipline across the wider team. What You Will Bring Significant experience (typically 6+ years) in project or program management, with a proven record of delivering regulatory change or remediation in a regulated financial services firm. Strong working knowledge of the Irish and/or UK regulatory environment, ideally including e-money, payments, AML/CFT and outsourcing or third-party oversight requirements. Experience engaging with, or preparing material for, the Central Bank of Ireland, FCA or equivalent supervisors. Demonstrable ability to manage multiple concurrent projects with competing deadlines and limited resources. Confident communicator with the credibility to influence senior stakeholders and the presence to hold cross-functional teams to account without needing direct line authority. Strong planning, risk management, and reporting skills, with a pragmatic risk-based and evidence-focused approach. Recognised project management qualification (e.g. PMP, PRINCE2, MSP) is desirable. Enhanced parental leave: 12 weeks for primary carers and 4 weeks for secondary carers. Private medical insurance fully covered by EML, including GP support, specialists, diagnostics and physiotherapy, plus optical, dental and hearing allowances. An Employee Assistance Programme with a 24/7 confidential helpline and up to 6 counselling sessions a year. A workplace pension scheme with company contributions 5% and employee minimum 3%. Income protection of up to 75% of salary and life insurance at 4× annual salary. A Cycle to Work scheme (up to €1,250). Support with one relevant professional membership a year. Our mission is to create awesome, instant, and secure payment solutions that connect our customers to their customers, anytime, anywhere, wherever money is in motion. Our Purpose is to inspire transformative digital change for our customers and communities. As an issuer and processor, we provide our clients and partners with innovative alternatives to traditional banking solutions for reloadable and non-reloadable programs. Our commitment to Equal Employment Opportunity Integrated into our Core Values is EML's commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion. EML is committed to being a globally inclusive company where all people are treated fairly, recognised for their individuality, promoted based on performance and empowered to reach their full potential. We are agile, we are innovative. We take a partnership approach; we tailor solutions and place a strong focus on operational excellence. Our place is one of collaboration, teamwork & innovation. But, above all, it’s one that embraces difference. And rather than have you blend in, we want to help you unleash your full potential. Within this context, the Group provides tailored solutions to internal clients while bringing innovation to enhance operational efficiency. Coordinate the opening, maintenance, modification, and closure of institutional bank accounts, ensuring that account mandates, authorized signatories, inventories, and supporting documentation remain accurate and compliant with Bank policies and controls. Act as a regional focal point for banking operational matters, coordinating with correspondent banks, custodians, Country Offices, Treasury teams, Legal, Compliance, and other stakeholders to resolve issues and maintain continuity of financial transactions. Oversee the maintenance and validation of Standard Settlement Instructions and other critical banking reference data used for Treasury transactions across multiple currencies and jurisdictions. Experience: At least three years of relevant experience in institutional banking operations, treasury middle-office, or a comparable control/operations environment, with hands-on responsibility for executing and coordinating banking administration and documentation activities. Languages: Proficiency in Spanish and English, spoken and written, is required. Additional knowledge of French and Portuguese is preferable. Requirements Citizenship: IDB– National: You are either a citizen of Honduras or a citizen of one of our 48-member countries with residency or legal permit to work in Honduras. Health Insurance: IDB Group provides employees and eligible dependents with a robust medical benefits program that covers medical, dental, vision, preventive care, and prescription drugs. Pension plan: Defined benefit pension plan that provides financial security and support employees in planning for their future. On-site position with the occasional flexibility of teleworking. Health and well-being: Access to our Health Services Center that provides preventive care and health education for employees. Our culture At the IDB, we work so everyone brings their best and authentic selves to work while finding their purpose. Our people consistently strive for excellence, and we recognize and celebrate the impact of their contributions. In our efforts to drive innovation, we intentionally include all voices, cultivate a sense of belonging and champion fairness. We welcome individuals from underrepresented groups to join us and share their unique perspectives. We ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job interview process. review_candidates.description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Job Overview Across the U.S. and Europe, IRC's Resettlement, Asylum, and Integration (RAI) department works to strengthen the systems that surround newcomers, building the capacity of service providers, governments, and communities to plan, coordinate, and deliver services more effectively. Over the past decade, this work has reached tens of thousands of learners through more than 50 projects across 13 countries and all 50 U.S. states. The IRC is seeking a Program Officer to support the implementation of Catalyst, RAI’s new systems strengthening identity. Catalyst draws on IRC's expertise in learning, research, programmatic excellence, partnerships, and AI-enabled delivery to help governments and organizations build stronger, more coordinated systems that deliver accessible, high-quality services to newcomers. Through systems strengthening work, Catalyst advances RAI's Impact@Scale priorities of Legal Services, Workforce Development, and Connected Communities. This role will focus on project management and coordination of various Catalyst systems strengthening projects. The position will lead cross-team coordination among multiple contributors, support strategy and outreach efforts, manage deliverables using Switchboard’s project management tools, and ensure timely, high-quality completion of work across multiple initiatives. This role reports to the Senior Program Officer for Catalyst and will work closely with teams across Switchboard and the IRC. Major Responsibilities Serve as the designated project manager for state-specific training and capacity-building initiatives. Manage projects across multiple teams, establishing clear processes, tracking progress, and ensuring deliverables meet internal standards, established deadlines, and funder expectations. Identify risks and adapt plans to ensure project goals are met in evolving contexts. Contribute technical expertise by developing and delivering trainings, providing consultations, and producing written materials aligned with state-identified needs and priority topic areas. Cultivate and manage relationships with internal teams and external partners, serving as a point of contact to sustain effective collaboration. Support outreach and partnership development for emerging opportunities and assist senior leadership in identifying and pursuing new initiatives. Collaborate with the Monitoring & Evaluation team to ensure accurate data collection, analysis, reporting, and documentation of outcomes, lessons learned, and promising practices. Other duties as assigned. Job Requirements Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree in Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Social Work, International Affairs, or a related field preferred. 3+ years of experience in program or project management. Demonstrated experience in assessing and building organizational capacity, monitoring and evaluation, and managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects. Proven ability to liaise effectively with multiple stakeholders, including government agencies (federal, state, and municipal), nonprofit organizations, educational institutions, the business sector, and community groups. Strong familiarity with relevant Office of Refugee Resettlement (ORR)-funded programs and services, with an emphasis on state-administered programming Familiarity with grant-funded programming and federal funding requirements undefined Skills and Competencies Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously. Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with a track record of effective collaboration across diverse teams. Strategic thinker with attention to detail and a solutions-oriented approach. Ability to remain calm, flexible, and effective in a fast-paced environment. Proficiency in project management tools and Microsoft Office Suite (experience with Airtable preferred).
